claim: A nationally weighted US survey of 5,034 podcast consumers found 32% of everyone who ever started making a podcast has since stopped (lapsed), constituting a lapsed-creator population equal to 50% the size of the active creator base.
stance_target: existence of a real exit/lapsed-creator survey instrument for content creators
scope_conditions: US adults 18+, podcast creators/consumers only, fielded December 2025
quoted_support: "1 in 3 creators who started have stopped ... Retention Rate: 68% Churn Rate: 32%"

claim: Despite the stated methodology including asking respondents about 'reasons for starting or stopping,' the published report does not present any directly self-reported reasons why lapsed creators quit; its explanatory 'format friction' mechanism is inferred from demographic-proxy matching, not measured directly.
stance_target: the corpus-wide absence of a genuine exit-survey instrument that captures why creators quit in their own words
scope_conditions: US podcast creators, 2025 Sounds Profitable survey
quoted_support: "Format data for lapsed creators was not captured directly; this analysis infers likely production format from demographic patterns."

claim: The report's authors explicitly identify 'what specific factors drive creator abandonment' and 'how does monetization affect sustainability' as open, unanswered research questions after analyzing their own lapsed-creator data.
stance_target: the absence of a money-vs-motivation exit-driver dataset even in the best available lapsed-creator sample
quoted_support: "What specific factors drive creator abandonment? ... How does monetization affect sustainability?"

claim: Churn rate among podcast creators varies from 23% (Asian) to 40% (age 55+ and LGBTQ+), a nearly 2x spread across demographic subgroups, within the same overall 32% churn population.
stance_target: demographic heterogeneity in creator attrition rates
quoted_support: "Churn rates vary from 23% to 40%—different demographics face different sustainability challenges"

claim: The gender gap in podcast creation is concentrated at the entry stage, not the retention stage: men are nearly twice as likely as women to become active creators (15% vs 8%), but once active, women retain at a comparable or slightly higher rate than men (69% vs 67%).
stance_target: whether attrition drivers differ from entry-barrier drivers
quoted_support: "The gender gap appears concentrated at entry, not sustainability"

claim: The report is industry-sponsored vendor research (every slide marked 'Sponsored by,' sponsor unnamed in extracted text) rather than peer-reviewed academic work, raising methodology-transparency concerns for citation reliability.
stance_target: epistemic tier / reliability of the best-available lapsed-creator survey
quoted_support: "Sponsored by" appears on every content page of the deck; sponsor entity not identified in the extracted text
